subject: general
question: Pooja, Harsh, and Madhur invest ₹1,120, ₹1,320, and ₹1,160, respectively to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹1,080, then what is the share of Madhur in the profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit distribution ratio = Ratio of **investments** (since time is constant).

Ratio of **Pooja** : **Harsh** : **Madhur** = 1120 : 1320 : 1160 = 28 : 33 : 29.

Total ratio parts = 28 + 33 + 29 = 90 units.

90 units = ₹1,080 ⇒ 1 unit = 1080 ÷ 90 = ₹12.

**Madhur share** = 29 units × 12 = ₹348.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹348.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Pooja investment** = ₹1,120, **Harsh investment** = ₹1,320, **Madhur investment** = ₹1,160. Total Profit = ₹1,080.

Formulas: Profit Share = (Individual Investment × Time) ÷ (Total Investment × Time) × Total Profit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fdc3a7cd8f8ef07ab1124d3ee7fc4e11212cf2fb48448b4e8a3907b294fccb18.png] 

⇒ **Total Investment** = 1120 + 1320 + 1160 = ₹3,600.

⇒ **Madhur share** = (1160 ÷ 3600) × 1080.

⇒ **Madhur share** = (29 ÷ 90) × 1080.

⇒ **Madhur share** = 29 × 12 = ₹348.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹348.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Ratios

When multiple partners invest for the same time period, the **Profit Ratio** is directly proportional to their **Capital Ratio**.

Variable Time Investment

If time periods differ, Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).
